quote:
* I also want to make the argument that while relationships are not strictly transactional, it would make no sense to completely ignore the pleasure created by a relationship. If either of your pleasure is at the explicit suffering of another, then it seems like you should reconsider such an arrangement. You can choose to give a part of yourself, but you have to be okay with that and actively choose it, not have it be chosen for you or just slid into.
   * Some people you are in a relationship may not have the abilities to consider or take seriously your pleasure or pleasure beyond themselves which in that case makes it much harder to sustain a positive hedonic relationship with them.
* Culture is currently caught between two opposing philosophies both of which make good points but of course lack nuance. On one side is “You don’t owe anyone your time/energy” and the other is “Inconvenience is the cost of community”. What is the appropriate cost to bear and what do we owe each other? At the very least we owe politeness and common decency if we are both on common ground. However beyond that I feel like it becomes tricky. Each person’s internal calculus will be different but I think it’s most helpful to think that you can’t complain about doing things for friends
